Title: Polygon Lasso Selection
Content: Objective Select Patterns, Sewing Lines, Topstitches, and Puckering with more freedom. Location Main Menu Edit tool for the respective item 3D/ 2D Toolbar Edit tool for the respective item Note: Edit Tools for Respective Items Pattern Transform Pattern (A) Line/Point Edit Pattern (Z) Sewing Edit Sewing (B) Topstitches Edit Topstitch (J) Buttons/Buttonholes Select/Move Button () Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Edit tool for the respective item 3D/ 2D Toolbar Edit tool for the respective item Double click in the 2D window, then drag the mouse. A selection point appears where the mouse is double clicked and a line follows as the mouse is dragged. The Transform pattern tool's selection box can now select patterns no matter the area it covers by holding CTRL and clicking and dragging your mouse. (ver. 2024.0) Click around the items to create the lasso selection. Click on the start point to complete the lasso selection. All items related to the Edit tool are selected and highlighted in yellow. Note: Only items related to the activated Edit tool are selected. For example, if the Edit Pattern tool is used to create a polygon lasso selection, only segments and points within the lasso selection are selected.

Title: Transform Point/Segment
Content: Objective Transform a Pattern by scaling or rotating its point and segment. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Transform Point/Segment 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern tool (hold down the button) Transform Point/Segment Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Transform Point/Segment 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern tool (hold down the button) Transform Point/Segment Select the point/segment to be transformed. The selected point/segment is highlighted in yellow and the surrounding marquee box appears. The Transform pattern tool's selection box can now select patterns no matter the area it covers by holding CTRL and clicking and dragging your mouse. (ver. 2024.0) Move, scale, or rotate the selected point/segment. The Pattern is transformed as the selected points/segments are edited.

Title: Cut/ Cut & Sew
Content: Objective Cut a single 2D Pattern into two or more pieces using Internal Lines (ver2.3.0). Location Transform Pattern/ Edit Pattern Tool Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern Trace Tool (ver2.4.0) Main Menu 2D Pattern Trace 2D Toolbar Trace Operation Transform Pattern/ Edit Pattern Tool Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern Right click on the Internal Line/Shape to access the pop-up menu. Then, select Cut or Cut &amp Sew. The Pattern is divided based on the selected Internal Line/Shape. If you select Cut &amp Sew, Sewing Lines are established between the divided Patterns. Trace Tool Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Trace 2D Toolbar Trace Right click on the Internal Line/Shape to access the pop-up menu. Then, select Cut or Cut &amp Sew. The Pattern is divided based on the selected Internal Line/Shape. If you select Cut &amp Sew, Sewing Lines are established between the divided Patterns. Note: With the Trace tool, you can Cut or Cut &amp Sew Patterns using the Baselines as well.

Title: Fold Pattern
Content: Objective Use this function to create a pressing effect by adjusting the angle of Pattern's Internal Line, for instance, pressed lines of formal trousers, fold direction of pleats. Location Pattern Property Editor Fold Fold Angle Operation Click on an Internal Line with Transform Pattern or Edit Pattern. Follow the indicated guideline below: Pattern Property Editor Fold Fold Angle Adjust the value of Fold Angle as desired. Note: Fold Strength Sets the angle closer as the value increases. The value range is in between 0 to 20. Fold Angle Sets the value in the range of 0 to 360, 180 represents a flat state. The internal line is folded towards the front of the pattern as the fold angle is closer to 0, and is folded into the back of the pattern as the angle is closer to 360. Fold Rendering Sets whether the pleats to have soft or sharp edges according to user preference. (Only applicable if Fold Arrangement is used on an Internal line.)

Title: Change Length
Content: Objective Type in the segment length and edit Pattern. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern Right click on the segment to be adjusted to access the pop-up menu. Then, select Change Length. The Change Length window appears. Enter the length of the segment and select the desired location. The preview shows in the 2D window. Click OK. The segment length is changed accordingly. Note: If a line connected to the selected line is a curve, the curve point is moved according to the changed length. If the "Lock Curve Points" option is checked, only straight points can be moved. (ver MD10)

Title: Steam
Content: Objective Shrink or stretch Fabric partially like as using a steam iron. Location Main Menu Materials Steam Steam 2D Toolbar Steam Operation Steam Setting Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Steam Steam 2D Toolbar Steam All Patterns are now being displayed in mesh. The Steam Brush appears at the top-left corner of the 2D window. Set the value as desired. Shrinkage Sets the shrinkage level. Size Sets the size of the brush. Hardness Sets the hardness of the steam. Click and drag on desired area to steam. According to the shrinkage, the selected area is now being displayed in light-blue or orange. Activate the Simulate. Remove Steam Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Steam Steam 2D Toolbar Steam Right-click on a pattern to remove steam, and select either Remove Steam on Selected Pattern or Remove All Steam. The steam is now being deleted accordingly. Note: It can also be removed from the same right-click pop-up menu with Edit Pattern or Transform Pattern tools.

Title: Divide Internal Lines
Content: Objective Cut and separate Internal Lines or points from an Internal Shape or continuous Internal Line. Location Divide Internal Point Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on Internal Point) Divide Internal Point Divide Internal Line Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on Internal Line) Divide Internal Line Operation Divide Internal Point Select the Edit Pattern tool from the 2D toolbar. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on Internal Point) Internal Point The Internal Line is divided at the selected point. The divided point is now indicated as a point with no fill. Divide Internal Line Select the Edit Pattern tool from the 2D toolbar. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on Internal Line) Divide Internal Line The Internal Line is divided from its original Internal Shape. Title: History Window
Content: Objective Keep track of your workflow with the History window and revert to previous points at any given time. In addition, save 3D states to review and compare specific points of progress. Location 3D State History Window 3D State Delete &amp Rename Right-click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D State) Delete or Rename Operation 3D State Follow the indicated guideline below: History Window 3D State Double click the desired 3D State. Warning as follows appears: "Loading the 3D State will delete the current History. Would you like to proceed?" Select OK. The 3D garment is reverted to the selected 3D State. Delete &amp Rename Follow the indicated guideline below: Right-click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D State) Delete or Rename The name field is highlighted and name can be changed. The selected 3D State is deleted. You can find a preview window if hovering your mouse over the thumbnail of a desired '3D State' file. (ver. 12.2)

Title: Avatar Materials
Content: Objective Edit avatar color, texture image, and opacity. Location 3D Toolbar Select/Move Select Avatar Property Editor Materials (Selected) Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar Select/Move Select Avatar Property Editor Materials (Selected) Adjust individual properties below. Diffuse Color Sets the color of avatars. Diffuse Map Applies image files on avatar surfaces. The diffuse color overlays on top of the applied image file. Ambient Color Sets the Ambient Color of avatars. Ambient Map Applies image files on avatar surfaces. The ambient color overlays on top of the applied image file. Specular Color Sets the Specular Color of avatars. Specular Map Applies image files on avatar surfaces. The Specular Color overlays on top of the applied image file. Shininess Sets the depth of sheen applied to the Specular Color, ranging from soft sheen to plastic-like gloss. Emission Color Sets the Emission Color of avatars. Opacity Sets the transparency of avatars. Note: Changes made to the Materials (Selected) properties can be saved at Main Menu File Save As Avatar (ver2.5.0). After the modification, it is possible to undo it by pressing (Ctrl+Z) (ver3.0.0).

Title: Show Simulation Speed (Below ver.12.1)
Content: Objective Check Simulation Speed of CLO on device in use. Recommended Simulation Speed for running CLO is between 25 and 30 FPS when simulating the pre-loaded default garment. Location Main Menu Display Environment Show Frame Rate Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Display Environment Show Frame Rate The Simulation Speed displays at the bottom-left corner of the 3D window. Note: The Simulation Speed is measured when the simulation is on. The higher the value of FPS (Frames per Second), the faster the simulation speed.

Title: Proxy Server Setting
Content: * Note Marvelous Designer has removed the Proxy Server option from version 11 and onward, in order to enhance the security for users. If users however, wish to continue using the Proxy Server in their network system, then please refer below. Objective Set the proxy server through environment variables provided by the OS * Note: Only HTTP/HTTPS protocol is supported. Operation 1. Click the start button on the taskbar. 2. Click Edit environment variables. 3. Environment Variables System Variable Click the New... and enter the proxy server information Information When using IP When Using User ID/ Password Variable name PROXY_HTTP (Capital letter) * Note: When connecting to a proxy server using HTTPS, the variable name must be entered as PROXY_HTTPS. Variable value ip:port E.g) 12.34.56.78:80 Id:password@url:port E.g) MD:password123@example.com:8080 * Note: On Mac, you need to enter environment variables in Shell Profile. (Bash Shell: ~/.bash_profile, Z Shell: ~/.zprofile)

Title: Select Mesh (Brush) (Above ver. 9)
Content: Select Area Objective Use the select Mesh (Brush) tool to select the area you want Location Main Menu 3D Garment Select Mesh (Brush) 3D Window Toolbar Select Mesh (Brush) Operation Follow the path specified in Location. Set the desired intensity, size, and focal of the brush in the brush dialog. You can adjust the brush size using the shortcut on the keyboard. Click on the desired part of the garment click and drag to select an area. When using the brush, you can see that the border is gradated according to the set intensity and focus. The area marked with dark green in the center is the area with 100% value, and the applied value gets smaller as it goes outward. The area becomes darker as you drag multiple times. Press and hold hotkeys below to add/ delete the selection area. Shift Key: Toggle between the existing selection area. Shift+Ctrl key: The Selection area will be added unconditionally. Ctrl Key: The Selection area will be deleted unconditionally. Right-click on the selection area Select Menu. The menu is also available in Select Mesh (Box) and Select Mesh (Lasso). Subdivision Right click on selection area Select "Subdivide" menu. Can use the "Subdivide menu" with Select Mesh (Box), Select Mesh (Lasso) as well. The mesh of the selected area is divided twice. Select Generated subdivision area can be selected with the Select Mesh (Brush) tool and the Select/Move tool. Delete Press "Delete" Key after selecting subdivision to delete a subdivision area. Property setting Select a subdivision area to display the property setting window. 1. Name: Set the name of selected subdivision area. 2. Level: Subdivision level 1 (Default) divide mesh twice. Higher the level, the more the mesh divides into multiples. Show/Hide Show/Hide generated subdivision area by Main menu Display 3D garment Show Subdivision. Partial Freeze Right-click on the selection area Select Freeze Menu. The menu is also available in Select Mesh (Box) and Select Mesh (Lasso). The mesh of the selected area is freezed. Select The created freeze area can be selected with the Select Mesh (Brush) tool and the Select/Move tool. Delete After selecting the freeze area, you can delete it by pressing the Delete key on your keyboard. Freeze area right click select/delete menu - Delete Freeze Region: Delete the selected freeze area. - Delete All Freeze: Delete all freeze areas. - Select All Freeze: Select all freeze areas. 3D Pattern right click select/delete menu Right-click on the 3D pattern to use the Partial Freeze menus. - Select All Freeze: Select all freeze areas. - Delete All Freeze: Delete all freeze areas. Move The created freeze area can be selected and moved with the Select / Move tool. Partial Solidify (Above ver. 11) Right-click on the selection area Select Solidify Menu. The menu is also available in Mesh Select (Box) and Mesh Select (Lasso). The mesh of the selected area is solidified. Select The created solidify area can be selected with the Select Mesh (Brush) tool and the Select/Move tool. Delete After selecting the solidify area, you can delete it by pressing the Delete key on your keyboard. Solidify area right click select/delete menu - Delete Solidify Region: Delete the selected solidify area. - Delete All Solidify: Delete all solidify areas. - Select All Solidify: Select all solidify areas. 3D Pattern right click select/delete menu Right-click on the 3D pattern to use the Partial Solidify menus. - Select All Solidify: Select all solidify areas. - Delete All Solidify: Delete all solidify areas.

Title: Layer Clone
Content: Objective Create an instance of the Pattern in its 3D state while sewing its Pattern outlines and Internal Lines to its instance's Pattern outlines and Internal Lines. Use the function to easily create padded jackets, collars, cuffs and other garments/details made with multiple layers of Patterns. Location Right Click Pop-Up Menu Layer Clone (Over/Under) Operation Select Transform Pattern tool or Edit Pattern tool. Select the Patterns to be layer cloned. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu Layer Clone (Over) The cloned Pattern is placed above the original Pattern. Right Click Pop-Up Menu Layer Clone (Under) The cloned Pattern is placed beneath the original Pattern. Activate Simulation. The cloned layer is simulated based on the option selected.

Title: Create Buttonhole
Content: Objective Create buttonholes and place them as desired. Location Main Menu Materials Button Buttonhole 3D Toolbar Buttonhole Operation Create Buttonhole Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Button Buttonhole 3D Toolbar Buttonhole Click on a desired point on the 3D Garment or 2D Pattern. A buttonhole is created. Enter the number of garment layers and click OK. The buttonholes are now being created. Input Measurement for Buttonhole Position Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Button Buttonhole 3D Toolbar Buttonhole Right-click on the 2D pattern where buttonholes would be placed. The Moving Distance window appears. Input desired measurements for accurate placement. Placement preview depending on the input value displays along the mouse in the 2D window. Click OK to place. The buttonholes are now being created.

Title: Apply Texture
Content: Objective Apply 2D image files to express the surface texture of Fabric. Operation via Drag and Drop Open a folder that contains the desired texture image in your file browser. Drag and drop the texture image onto a pattern in the 2D or 3D window. The texture of all patterns using the same Fabric will have the new texture applied. Note: If a texture image is already applied, the existing texture image will be replaced when applying a new texture image via drag and drop. Drag and drop an image file directly from the file browser to the Open icon next to the Texture menu in the Property Editor (ver4.0.0). Drag and drop an image file directly from the file browser to an object in the program, then select the correct map: texture, normal, specular (ver4.0.0). via Property Editor Select a Fabric to apply a texture image to from the Fabric tab in the Object Browser. Follow the path: Property Editor Material Texture Open button. The Open File window appears. Find and select the desired texture image from the file browser, then load. The selected texture image is now applied to the Fabric.

Title: Optimize Curve Points
Content: Objective Optimize the number of curve points on Patterns and Internal Lines to ease the Pattern editing process (ver3.0.0). Optimize Curve Points dialog appears, and the number of curve points is automatically applied as an optimized ratio. (ver.7.3.0) Curve Points Adjust the ratio of curve points by a percentage (%). The closer to 0% it is, the fewer curve points there will be. But there may be deviations from the original curvature. Reset Reset the applied ratio of curve points while the dialog is running. Apply Apply the Optimize Curve Points based on the input ratio. Close Close the Optimize Curve Points dialog. Right-click your mouse on the desired patterns or segments, and select Optimize Curve Points. Optimize Curve Points dialog appears, and the number of curve points is automatically applied as an optimized ratio. (ver.7.3.0) Curve Points Adjust the ratio of curve points by a percentage (%). The closer to 0% it is, the fewer curve points there will be. But there may be deviations from the original curvature. Reset Reset the applied ratio of curve points while the dialog is running. Title: Project with Meta Data (*.ZPrj)/ Garment with Meta Data (*.zpac)
Content: Objective When saving Project files, an accompanying XML file with Garment, trim, and texture information will be provided. Turntable images will also be generated with the Project file (versions after 3.1.38) XML File Contents 1. Product version 2. Garment version 3. Garment polygon, triangle, vertex count: this includes the pattern, trims, textures all information related to the Garment. 3-1. Pattern polygon, triangle, vertex count 3-2. Trim Object polygon, triangle, vertex count: Trim are Object files imported via File Import Import as Trim. 3-3. Button polygon, triangle, and vertex count 3-4. Print Texture polygon, triangle, vertex count: Print Texture are textures imported as Graphic. 3-5. Texture Count: the number of textures applied to Fabric. 3-6. Material Count: the number of items used or applied to Fabric. 4. Avatar total polygon, triangle, and vertex count 5. Turntable image names Location Save as Project: Main Menu Save As Project with Metadata/ Garment with Meta Data Operation Save as Project Navigate to the menu listed in Location. Save File window will appear. Navigate to the desired file location. Enter a file name in File Name, then click the Save button. The Save Metadata dialogue will appear. File Save Folder Saves the Project file along with the metadata and turntable images within a folder. Save .zip File Saves the Project file along with the metadata and turntable images as a ZIP file. Image Image Count Select the number of images for the Turntable. * Don't Show Again Check Box Checking this box will hide the dialog, but will remember the last entered settings when saving the metadata. To view the dialog again, go to Main Menu User Settings Others Metadata, then set the Don't Show Again Save Metadata option to Off.

Title: ZIPPER: Create Zippers
Content: Objective Create and use Zippers quickly and easily. Location Main Menu Materials Zipper Zipper 3D Toolbar Zipper Operation Navigate to the location listed below: 3D Toolbar Zipper Click on the 3D garment or 2D Patterns (ver MD10) where the Zipper should be attached, then move the cursor. Based on the direction the cursor is moved, the segment where the Zipper appears is highlighted in light blue. Double click on the desired endpoint for the Zipper. One side of the Zipper is created. Click on the Pattern outline where the other side of the Zipper is attached, then move the cursor. Based on the direction the cursor is moved, a blue point appears indicating the same length as the first half of the Zipper which was created in step 3. Double click on the blue point. The Zipper is now complete, along with a Puller, Slider, and Stopper (ver MD10). Activate the Simulation. The Zipper simulates in a closed/fully zipped state. To unzip the Zipper, click on the Zipper in the 3D Window WITHOUT the Gizmo active, and drag to move the Zipper (referenced in dark grey) along the length of the Zipper Tape. Note: Cancel Actions during Zipper Creation Cancel All Actions While using the Zipper tool, press 'Esc' or 'Ctlr +Z' on the keyboard, and all actions will be undone. Cancel Last Action While using the Zipper tool, press the 'Delete' or 'Backspace' Key on the keyboard and the last action will be undone.

Title: Why do I have to pay tax?
Content: Please note that if you have a correct registered VAT ID, you can add VAT ID on Billing Address and your tax will be waived Since January 2019, CLO Virtual Fashion LLC(Marvelous Designer US office) has officially been registered VAT MOSS(Sales Tax) in Ireland(EU). - Since our online license sales are handled by our US office, all of our Individual license pricing will be in effect, according to the regulation below. From January 2015, new legislation came into force that affects the sale of digital services to customers in other EU countries. Digital services include broadcasting, telecommunications, and electronic services(which includes software products). The VAT rate that is calculated for this type of transaction is based on a place of supply the service. The legislation that is regulating MOSS rules is: Council Directive (EU) 2017/2455 - supplies of services and distance sales of goods (VAT e-commerce package). Council Directive 2008/8/EC - a place of supply of services. Council Implementing Regulation (EU) No 1042/2013 - place of supply of services. This means if your billing address is under the EU region, VAT rates for each country will be added to your purchase. Austria 20% Belgium 21% Bulgaria 20% Czech Republic 21% Denmark 25% Germany 19% Estonia 20% Ireland 23% Greece 24% Spain 21% France 20% Croatia 25% Italy 22% Cyprus 19% Latvia 21% Lithuania 21% Luxembourg 17% Hungary 27% Malta 18% Netherlands 21% Poland 23% Portugal 23% Romania 19% Slovenia 22% Slovakia 20% Finland 24% Sweden 25% UK 20% If you would like to discover more regarding VAT MOSS, please review the file attached.

Title: Compatible File Format
Content: Compatible File Format File Format Import Export Detail 3D FBX *.fbx O O File contains Mesh, Material, Joint, Animation, and Camera information. *Only Joint that was imported as FBX to Marvelous Designer can be exported as FBX. Open COLLADA *.dae O X This file can be exported from other 3D softwares such as 3ds Max, Maya and used. These files contain geometry and material, also in a addition to rigging, skinning, and animation data When exporting OpenCOLLADA files from 3DS Max or Maya, install the OpenCOLLADA plugin (http://www.opencollada.org) and export to use the avatar OBJ *.obj O O File contains Geometry and Material Information. Primarily used for importing Avatar and related sources into the program. LXO *.lxo X O File contains Geometry and Material Information. Used to export Apparel/Avatar information to Modo in the LXO file format. Animation Cache *.mc *.pc2 *.mdd O O Is the vertex animation data. It is possible to take animations made in Marvelous Designer to 3DSMax or Maya in point cache format. Alembic *.abc O O Is an interchange file format for computer graphics that saves both vertex and animation information. Mac export (ver. 5.1.431) 3D Snapshot *.png - O Ability to save single views of the 3D window in the PNG file format. 2D Texture *.jpg, *.png, etc. O O Textures inserted into garments, use image textures in formats such as JPG, PNG, TIF, and PSD. Supported file types: jpg, jpeg, png, bmp, wbmp, psd, ico, tga, tif, tiff, gif, mng, jng, dds, hdr, koa, lbm, iff, pbm, pcd, pcx, pgm, ppm, ras, cut, xmb, xpm, sgi, g3, exr, j2k, jp2, pfm, pict, pct) Substance .sbsar O - File contains procedural texture information with adjustable parameters. The separate channels of a Substance material can be baked and exported (color, normal, metalness, roughness, opacity)

Title: Zoom In/Out, Rotation
Content: Objective In Marvelous Designer, the mouse wheel and the right button can be used to zoom in, zoom out, and rotate the screen. The Maya and 3Ds Max view control methods are also supported alongside the default view control method and interface can be modified as needed and use differently. Operation Move Hold down the mouse wheel and drag to move the screen. If you are using Mac's Magic Mouse, please hold down the Alt key on the keyboard and click-and-drag the left mouse key. Zoom In/Out Scroll down (zoom in) and up (zoom out) the mouse wheel to zoom in and zoom out the screen. Or, hold down Alt Key on the keyboard and the left button of the mouse simultaneously and drag up (zoom out) or down (zoom in). Note: Zoom in or zoom out using the + (zoom in) and - (zoom out) keys on the keyboard (ver2.4.0.) Rotate Hold down the right button of the mouse and drag to rotate the 3D window.
